chunks: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad al-Ṭāhirī, who said:

Al-Mutawakkil became ill from an abscess that appeared on him, and because of it he came near to destruction. No one dared to touch him with iron. So his mother vowed that if he were cured, she would carry to Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام a great amount from her wealth. Al-Fatḥ ibn Khāqān said to him, “If only you would send to this man and ask him, for it may well be that he has a description of a remedy by which relief may come to you.”

So he sent to him عليه السلام and described his illness to him. The messenger returned to him with the instruction that the pressed residue of sheep fat should be taken, mixed with rosewater, and applied to it. When the messenger returned and informed them, they began mocking his statement. Al-Fatḥ said to him, “By Allah, he is more knowledgeable concerning what he said.” So the residue was brought, and it was prepared as he had said and applied to it. Sleep overcame him and he became calm. Then it opened and what had been inside it came out, and his mother was given glad tidings of his recovery.

So she carried to him عليه السلام ten thousand dinars under her seal. Then he recovered from his illness, and al-Baṭḥāʾī al-ʿAlawī informed against him that wealth and weapons were being carried to him عليه السلام. So he said to Saʿīd the chamberlain, “Attack him at night, take whatever wealth and weapons you find with him, and bring it to me.”

Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad said: Saʿīd the chamberlain said to me, “I went to his house at night, and I had with me a ladder. I climbed to the roof, and when I descended partway down the steps in the darkness, I did not know how to reach the house. Then he called to me, ‘O Saʿīd, stay where you are until they bring you a candle.’ It was not long before they brought me a candle. So I descended and found that he was wearing a woolen cloak and a woolen cap, and there was a sajjādah upon a mat before him. I had no doubt that he was performing salat (prayer).”

He said to me, ‘The rooms are before you.’ So I entered them and searched them, but I found nothing in them. I found the purse in his house sealed with the seal of the mother of al-Mutawakkil, and another sealed bag. He said to me, ‘The place of salat (prayer) is before you.’ So I lifted it and found a sword in an unsheathed cover. I took that and went to him. When he looked at his mother’s seal on the purse, he sent for her and she came out to him.

Some of the special servants informed me that she said to him, ‘I had made a vow during your illness, when I had despaired for you, that if you recovered I would carry to him ten thousand dinars from my wealth. So I carried it to him, and this is my seal on the bag.’ He opened the other bag and there were four hundred dinars in it. So he added to the purse another purse and ordered me to carry that to him عليه السلام. So I carried it, and I returned the sword and the two bags, and I said to him, ‘O my master, this weighed heavily upon me.’
So he said to me: “And those who have done ظلم will come to know to what overturning they shall be overturned.”

key_terms.الْبَدْرَةَ: a purse or bag of money
key_terms.الْمُصَلَّى: the place of salat (prayer) or prayer rug
key_terms.خَاتَمِهَا: her seal or signet used to mark the bag
key_terms.خُرَاجٍ: an abscess or boil causing severe illness
key_terms.ظَلَمُوا: they acted unjustly or committed oppression
key_terms.كُسْبُ الشَّاةِ: the pressed residue or extract from sheep fat used as a remedy
key_terms.نَذَرَتْ: she made a vow contingent upon recovery

ai.seo_question: How does the hadith about al-Mutawakkil’s illness show the knowledge and dignity of Imam ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This report narrates the illness of al-Mutawakkil, his cure through the instruction of Imam ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام, and the later attempt to seize wealth and weapons from the Imam’s residence. It highlights the Imam’s knowledge, composure, and spiritual station, while ending with a Qur'anic warning concerning the fate of the oppressors.
